beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: How do you find ten more or ten less than a number? Start with forty-six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each small square is one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each rod is ten ones.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four tens and six ones make forty-six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: What is ten more than forty-six?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Add one rod. Five tens and the same six ones make fifty-six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Slide that rod away. Back to forty-six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: What is ten less than forty-six?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Remove one rod. Three tens and the same six ones make thirty-six. Only the tens digit changes.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: On a hundred chart, ten more is one step down: forty-six to fifty-six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Back to forty-six. Ten less is one step up: thirty-six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Down this column, the ones digit is always six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The model shows fifty. Take away twenty. What number is left?

do.text: The model shows $50$. Take away $20$. What number is left?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Fifty is five tens. Twenty is two tens, so take two rods away.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Five tens minus two tens is three tens, so fifty minus twenty is thirty.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: What is ten less than sixty-nine? Explain why.

do.text: What is ten less than $69$? Explain why.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Sixty-eight, sixty-seven... I've lost how many ones I took away.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: I'll use tens. Remove one rod. Five tens and nine ones. Fifty-nine.

do.text: Remove one ten. Keep nine ones.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten more adds a rod, so the tens digit goes up by one.

do.text: Ten more: tens digit up one

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten less takes a rod away, so it goes down by one.

do.text: Ten less: tens digit down one

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten more, one more rod. The ones stay.
